teaching_note: Define the lifecycle technical-measurement strategy and decision chain
Characterize probability distributions, tails, dependence, and stochastic performance
Establish data provenance, sampling validity, exploratory analysis, and measurement uncertainty
Use estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis, equivalence, and engineering significance
Design efficient experiments with factors, responses, noise, power, randomization, and blocking
Analyze factorial experiments, interactions, diagnostics, and confirmation evidence
Build and validate performance response models across use and environment
Analyze reliability, availability, maintainability, degradation, and censored evidence
Propagate uncertainty with analytic Monte Carlo simulation and sensitivity analysis
Quantify requirement compliance, technical margin, allocation risk, and design options
Update lifecycle evidence and decide among upgrade, replacement, retirement, or more information
Integrate, reproduce, challenge, and defend the lifecycle analytics decision
